title: The imperative: giving instructions
summary: Give orders, instructions and advice: habla, haz, siga, no vayas, dímelo.
focus: Affirmative and negative commands for tú, usted and ustedes, and where the pronouns go
content:
## Tú: borrow the él form

To tell a friend what to do, use the **él / ella** form of the present tense as a command:

| verb | él form | command |
|---|---|---|
| hablar | habla | **¡Habla más despacio!** |
| comer | come | **Come la sopa.** |
| escribir | escribe | **Escribe tu nombre.** |

Eight verbs have short, irregular **tú** commands: **di** (decir), **haz** (hacer), **ve** (ir), **pon** (poner), **sal** (salir), **sé** (ser), **ten** (tener), **ven** (venir).

- **Haz los deberes.** Do your homework.
- **Ven aquí y pon la mesa.** Come here and lay the table.
- **Sé bueno y di la verdad.** Be good and tell the truth.

## Usted and ustedes: the subjunctive forms

Commands to **usted** and **ustedes** use the **present subjunctive**. Take the present **yo** form, drop the **-o** and swap the vowel: **-ar** verbs take **-e**, and **-er / -ir** verbs take **-a**. An irregular **yo** stem (hago, pongo, digo, tengo, vengo, salgo) carries into every person.

| infinitive | yo | usted | ustedes |
|---|---|---|---|
| hablar | hablo | **hable** | **hablen** |
| comer | como | **coma** | **coman** |
| hacer | hago | **haga** | **hagan** |
| decir | digo | **diga** | **digan** |
| venir | vengo | **venga** | **vengan** |

**Ir** (**vaya**) and **ser** (**sea**) break the rule, and so do *estar* (*esté*), *dar* (*dé*) and *saber* (*sepa*). Spelling keeps the sound the same, so cruzar becomes **cruce** and llegar becomes **llegue**.

- **Siga todo recto, señor.** Go straight on, sir.
- **Pasen y siéntense.** Come in and sit down.

## Don't: no + subjunctive

Every negative command uses the subjunctive, **tú** included. Use **no** plus the subjunctive **tú** form, which ends in **-s**.

| affirmative tú | negative tú |
|---|---|
| habla | **no hables** |
| come | **no comas** |
| haz | **no hagas** |
| ve | **no vayas** |
| sé | **no seas** |
| pon | **no pongas** |

For **usted / ustedes** the form is the same with or without **no**: **coma / no coma**, **salgan / no salgan**.

- **No cruces la calle aquí.** Don't cross the street here.
- **No tengan miedo.** Don't be afraid.

For **vosotros**, the affirmative swaps the **-r** of the infinitive for **-d** (**hablad**, **comed**, **venid**). The negative is the subjunctive (**no habléis**, **no vengáis**).

## Pronouns: glued on or in front

Object and reflexive pronouns **attach** to an affirmative command, indirect before direct. A written accent keeps the stress where it was: **dímelo** (tell me it), **siéntate** (sit down), **póngalo** (put it), **mézclalo** (mix it).

In a negative command they go **before** the verb: **no me lo digas**, **no te sientes**, **no lo ponga ahí**.

Recipes and directions use commands a lot:

- **Corta la cebolla, añade el aceite y mézclalo todo.** Cut the onion, add the oil and mix it all.
- **Gire a la derecha y cruce la plaza.** Turn right and cross the square. (usted)
- **Siéntate y cuéntamelo.** Sit down and tell me about it.

With vosotros reflexives, the **-d** drops: **sentaos**, **levantaos**.

vocabulary.example: Corta la cebolla en trozos pequeños.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Cut the onion into small pieces.

vocabulary.example: Pon la cebolla en la sartén.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Put the onion in the frying pan.

vocabulary.example: Gire a la izquierda en el semáforo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Turn left at the traffic lights.

vocabulary.example: Siga todo recto hasta la plaza.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Go straight on to the square.

vocabulary.example: No cruces con el semáforo en rojo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Don't cross when the light is red.

quiz.prompt: A un amigo: ___ más despacio, por favor.
quiz.explanation: An affirmative tú command is the él form of the present: 'habla'. 'Hable' is for usted, 'hablad' for vosotros.
hints: Affirmative tú commands look like the él form.

quiz.prompt: Tú command: ___ (hacer) los deberes antes de cenar.
quiz.explanation: Hacer is one of the eight irregular tú commands: 'haz'.
hints: One of the eight short irregular tú commands: one syllable.

quiz.prompt: A un señor mayor (usted): ___ todo recto hasta la plaza.
quiz.explanation: Usted commands use the subjunctive, so sigo becomes siga. 'Sigue' is the tú command, and 'sigan' is ustedes.
hints: Start from the yo form: sigo.

quiz.prompt: Usted, negative: No ___ (añadir) la sal todavía.
quiz.explanation: For usted the form is the same with or without 'no': 'no añada'. Añadir is an -ir verb, so the vowel is -a.
hints: Usted forms never change between affirmative and negative.

quiz.prompt: A tu hermano: ___ al parque ahora, es muy tarde.
quiz.explanation: Negative tú commands use the subjunctive tú form: 'no vayas'. 'Ve' is only affirmative, and 'no vas' is a statement.
hints: A negative tú command is no plus the subjunctive form ending in -s.
The subjunctive of ir is vaya.

quiz.prompt: Replace 'la verdad' with a pronoun: Dime la verdad → ___.
quiz.explanation: Pronouns attach to an affirmative command, indirect (me) before direct (la), and an accent keeps the stress: 'dímela'.
hints: Glue the pronouns to the end.
Add an accent on the i.

quiz.prompt: Which negative command ('don't tell me it') is correct?
quiz.explanation: In a negative command the pronouns go before the verb, indirect before direct: 'no me lo digas'.
hints: In a negative command the pronouns go in front.

quiz.prompt: Receta (tú): ___ (cortar) la cebolla y añade el aceite.
quiz.explanation: The affirmative tú command of a regular -ar verb is the él form: 'corta'.
hints: Same as the él/ella present form.

quiz.prompt: A dos turistas (ustedes): ___ la calle en el semáforo.
quiz.explanation: Ustedes takes the subjunctive -en, and -zar verbs spell z as c before e: 'crucen'. 'Cruzan' is a statement, and 'cruce' is singular usted.
The reflexive pronoun attaches to the affirmative command (sienta + te) and a written accent keeps the stress: 'siéntate'.
hints: The stem changes from e to ie, then te attaches.

listening.meaning: Sit down here, next to me.
listening.note: The pronoun glues onto the command and needs an accent: siéntate.

listening.text: Corta dos tomates y una cebolla.
listening.meaning: Cut two tomatoes and an onion.

listening.text: No cruces la calle sin mirar.
listening.meaning: Don't cross the street without looking.
listening.note: A negative tú command uses the subjunctive: no cruces.

listening.text: No añadas más azúcar al café.
listening.meaning: Don't add more sugar to the coffee.
listening.note: New word: el azúcar = the sugar.

listening.text: Mézclalo todo y ponlo en la nevera.
listening.meaning: Mix it all and put it in the fridge.
listening.note: New word: la nevera = the fridge.

listening.text: Gire a la derecha en la segunda calle, señora.
listening.meaning: Turn right at the second street, madam.

listening.text: Siga todo recto, cruce la plaza y gire a la izquierda en el semáforo.
listening.meaning: Go straight on, cross the square and turn left at the traffic lights.

guide.tip: Stuck on an usted form? Say the yo form first (hago, pongo, digo), drop the -o and swap the vowel to get haga, ponga, diga.

conversations.title: Grandma's tortilla
conversations.scenario: Carmen is teaching her grandson Dani to make a Spanish omelette. She gives the orders, and he asks questions.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Dani, ven aquí. Hoy haces tú la tortilla.
lines.meaning: Dani, come here. Today you're making the tortilla.

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: OK! What do I do first?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Pela las patatas y córtalas en trozos pequeños. Y corta una cebolla.
lines.meaning: Peel the potatoes and cut them into small pieces. And cut an onion.

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: Do I put in a lot of oil?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sí, pon bastante aceite en la sartén, pero no lo calientes demasiado.
lines.meaning: Yes, put plenty of oil in the pan, but don't heat it too much.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Bate cuatro huevos, añade un poco de sal y mézclalo todo con las patatas.
lines.meaning: Beat four eggs, add a little salt and mix it all with the potatoes.

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: Do I turn it over now?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¡No, no le des la vuelta todavía! Espera dos minutos. Ten paciencia.
lines.meaning: No, don't turn it over yet! Wait two minutes. Be patient.
lines.note: no plus the subjunctive: no le des

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Abuela, siéntate y descansa. Yo me encargo.
lines.meaning: Grandma, sit down and rest. I'll take care of it.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Muy bien. Pero no te olvides de la sal.
lines.meaning: Very good. But don't forget the salt.

bites.title: Tú = the él form
bites.rule: To order a friend around, use the él/ella present form: habla, come, escribe. Eight commands are short and irregular: di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten, ven.
bites.example: Haz los deberes y pon la mesa.
bites.example_meaning: Do your homework and lay the table.

bites.title: Usted = subjunctive
bites.rule: Usted/ustedes commands use the present subjunctive: Take the yo form, drop the -o and swap the vowel: -ar verbs take -e, and -er/-ir verbs take -a. So hago becomes haga and pongo becomes ponga.

bites.title: No + subjunctive
bites.rule: Every negative command is subjunctive, tú included: no hables, no comas, no hagas, no vayas, no seas. Usted keeps the same form: no coma.

bites.title: Pronouns: on or in front
bites.rule: Pronouns glue onto affirmative commands with an accent (dímelo, siéntate) and go in front of negative ones (no me lo digas, no te sientes).
bites.example_meaning: Tell me about it. Don't tell me about it.

sorts.title: Tú or usted?
sorts.why: Tú commands look like the él present form. Usted commands are subjunctive, with the swapped vowel.

sorts.title: Regular or irregular tú command?
sorts.why: Only di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten and ven are irregular. Every other verb uses the él form.

sorts.title: Where is the pronoun?
sorts.why: Affirmative commands carry the pronouns on the end. Negative commands put them before the verb.

spots.why: Hacer has the irregular tú command haz. Hace is a statement (he does).
Señor García is usted, so the command is the subjunctive siga.

spots.sentence: No habla tan rápido, que no te entiendo.
spots.why: A negative tú command needs the subjunctive: no hables.
Negative commands put the pronouns in front: no me lo digas.

spots.sentence: Córtala en trozos y añades el aceite.
spots.why: Both verbs are tú commands. Añades is the present statement, and añade is the command.
Attaching -se moves the stress, so a written accent is needed: siéntense.

builds.text: Corta la cebolla y añade la sal.
builds.meaning: Cut the onion and add the salt.

builds.text: Haz los deberes antes de cenar.

builds.meaning: Sit down here and speak slowly.
